TotallyTurtles.us: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Green with Jealousy
In order to steal nuclear energy from a submarine, Krang creates a love potion which induces lovesickness in all of the Turtles - except Donatello, who does not eat the potion-laced pizza.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Return of the Fly

Intent on revenge against both the Turtles, Krang and Shredder, the Fly (alias Baxter Stockman) returns with a bug of a plan. While the Turtles are battling Shredder, the insect tries to exterminate the entire group!
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Mutagen Monster
The chemicals from two carriages in a train wreck unite to form a mutagen, and steers licking up the goo are transformed into a bull-headed monster.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Corporate Raiders From Dimension X
Shredder utilizes a hypnotizing device and creates zombies out of CEOs all over the city. Ultimately, the plan is to raise the Technodrome from the centre of the Earth.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Pizza By The Shred
In order to locate the Turtles' lair and destroy them, Shredder opens a pizza parlour. When the Turtles order a pizza, Shredder places a locator-tracking device on it disguised as an anchovy.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Super Bebop & Mighty Rocksteady
Krang creates Cybernetic Clones of Rocksteady, only ten times as strong and ten times as smart.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Blast From the Past
Shredder endeavours to enlist the aid of the ghost of Shibano-Sama, a noble warrior who lived hundreds of years ago, to destroy the Turtles.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Leatherhead: Terror of the Swamp
The Turtles go south to the swamps when their friends the Frogs -and Napoleon Bonafrog - are in trouble. The source of their predicament is Leatherhead, a half-human, half-alligator mutation.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Michelangelo's Birthday
It's Michelangelo's birthday - and his good buddies are pretending they're unaware of it.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Usagi Yojimbo

Shredder's Teleporter, which can teletransport objects to a pre­determined location, interferes with Donatello's transdimensional reception - and Usagi Yojimbo, a 14th century Samurai rabbit, pops out of the Turtles' screen.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Case of the Hot Kimono
The Case of the Hot Kimono
Agatha Marble helps the Turtles in their pursuit of Don Turtelli, including Splinter's treasured red robe - and holding Happy Hour News' April and Vernon prisoners.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Usagi, Come Home
Shredder has a hare-brained scheme to turn the rabbit from another dimension, Usagi Yojimbo, into an ally of his and an enemy of the Turtles.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Making of Metalhead
Krang creates Metalhead, an exact robot replica of the Turtles with even more powers, and directs him to destroy the Turtles. Donatello, however, reprograms Metalhead over to the Turtles' side.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Leatherhead Meets the Rat King
Leatherhead The Cajan gator goes into the sewers in pursuit of the Turtles, and encounters the Rat King, who has stolen a tanker­truck of rat poison which he plans to change into a hypnotic gas.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Turtle Terminator
Shredder captures Irma and creates an android Irma programmed to destroy the Turtles. The zap-happy robotic Irma causes havoc in the TV newsroom.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Great Boldini
Mobster Don Turtelli and his cousin the magician, the Great Baldini, steal the famous Tortellini Emerald.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Missing Map
The Turtles are showing Zach, "the fifth Turtle," and his brother Walt their scrapbook.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Gang's All Here
Michelangelo falls for a Shredder trick and eats a chocolate chip cookie made with anti-mutagen capable of turning him into a human being.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Grybyx
The Neutrinos - Dask, Kala and Zak - are back on Earth in search of Kala's pet Grybyx, a small and cuddly creature that, "mega bizzarro," can turn into a humongous monster.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Mister Ogg Goes to Town

When Krang realizes the Technodrome is running low on liquid nitrogen, its main source of fuel, he discovers that a formula exists in Dimension Z which transmutes crude oil, easily available on Earth, into liquid nitrogen.
Because of all the destruction Shredder causes just trying to get rid of the Turtles, they lament that the world would be a better place had they never existed.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Bye - Bye Fly!
Plotting revenge, Baxter, who has been turned into a fly-like creature, delivers a borellium crystal to Krang and Shredder whose Technodrome is low in power.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Big Ripoff
The Technodrome is perilously close to running out of power as it teeters on the edge of a crumbling lava cliff deep within the bowels of the Earth.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Big Break-In
Krang and Shredder get the Technodrome rolling again and raise it to the centre of the Earth.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Big Blow-Out
Krang and Shredder raise the Technodrome to the surface and seize unlimited energy. The Turtles and the World face their darkest hour.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Plan Six from Outer Space
The Turtles launch the missile from the sewers positioned under the Technodrome. It transports Bebop, Rocksteady, Krang and Shredder back to Dimension X but explodes on impact; they survive.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Turtles of the Jungle
Donatello's idol, inventor mad-scientist Professor Willard creates the Molecular Intensifier, a machine to control growth of living things.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Michelangelo Toys Around
Michelangelo dreams he's being attacked by Tyranno-toys. He wakes up to hear April announcing the Toy Fair opening. Determined to go, Michelangelo disguises himself as a Turtle toy.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Peking Turtles

April O'Neil reports from the Uptown Museum about a display of artifacts from the 2000-year-old Ying Dynasty of China. The marble warriors were built to protect the world's largest pearl from being stolen from the Emperor's collection of j…
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Shredder's Mother
The earth is experiencing global warming and Krang and Shredder threaten to expose it to increased catastrophic weather conditions.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Four Turtles and A Baby
The Neutrinos are attacked and their leaders, Zenter and Grizzla, are seized by Krang, Shredder and General Traag.

Widespread thievery is discovered in the city when Ninja Turtle artifacts are found missing. April and Irma prowl for the pilfering poachers, the investigation leads the reporter to the estate of Monroe Q.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Rondo in New York

Word spreads that Oswald Oren, a nerdy Woody Allen-type student, has developed the Vitalizer - an experimental substance that brings inanimate objects to life. Scoundrels Shredder, Krang, Bebop and Rocksteady connive to steal the potion.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Planet of the Turtles

A commercial for the Personal Energy Projector (PEP), allowing the transfer of energy from one source to another, entices Krang. Targeting Earth, he drains the sphere's energy to strengthen the Technodrome.
